extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy (philosophers, scholars, educated public)
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpt from a philosophy text that defines the nature and scope of Philosophy, distinguishes it from Science, sets methodological constraints on philosophical inquiry, and gives normative advice on toleration and the public expression of conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toleration and active recognition of positive worth
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our toleration therefore should be the widest possible. Or rather, we should aim at something beyond toleration... to do justice by an open recognition of positive worth. We must qualify our disagreement with as much as may be of sympathy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't merely refrain from injustice of word or deed toward alien beliefs; actively recognize their positive worth. Bear in mind three cardinal facts when dealing with other creeds: (1) every form of religion contains a 'soul of truth'; (2) concrete elements that embody that truth may be bad by an absolute standard but good relatively (they serve as 'protective envelopes'); (3) various beliefs are necessary, constituted parts of human social life and repeatedly reappear. Use these facts to temper condemnation, cultivate sympathy, and justify wide toleration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance progressive and conservative tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: "While it is requisite that free play should be given to conservative thought and action, progressive thought and action must also have free play... Without the agency of both, there cannot be those continual re-adaptations which orderly progress demands."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical and social reform should be balanced: conservatism supplies stabilizing adaptation to popular character, progress supplies necessary remodelling. Avoid extremes: rapid substitution of new forms invites violent retrogressions; gradual re-adaptation with both forces operating produces continuous growth. In practice, allow both conservative and progressive voices scope to influence change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy as completely-unified knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "Knowledge of the highest degree of generality... Knowledge of the lowest kind is un-unified knowledge; Science is partially-unified knowledge; Philosophy is completely-unified knowledge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat philosophical work as the project of integrating the widest generalizations of the sciences into unified, higher-order propositions. Philosophy is not merely another separated scientific truth: it consolidates and interprets the broadest scientific generalizations (examples given: dynamics of fluids/solids, relations of temperature and oxygenation, economic generalizations) into a comprehensively unified account. Avoid calling unsystematized or narrowly detailed knowledge 'philosophical.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Philosophy to the relative; avoid claims about the Unknowable
rubrics_metrics.description: "After concluding that we cannot know the ultimate nature of that which is manifested to us, there arise the questions — What is it that we know? ... The range of intelligence we find to be limited to the relative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical inquiry should confine itself to what human intelligence can legitimately reach (the relative and integrative knowledge of phenomena), not to speculative Ontology about the ultimate nature of 'The Unknowable.' Consequently, philosophy should work by integrating scientific knowledge rather than claiming transcendent, absolute knowledge beyond manifestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two forms: General Philosophy and Special Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Two forms of Philosophy... On the one hand, the things contemplated may be the universal truths: all particular truths referred to being used simply for proof or elucidation of these universal truths. On the other hand... the things contemplated may be the particular truths as interpreted by them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish work that seeks and formulates universal truths (General Philosophy) from work that applies those universals to interpret particulars (Special Philosophy). In General Philosophy universals are the products of exploration; in Special Philosophy they are instruments of exploration. State which mode your philosophical project adopts and structure arguments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the isolated-datum fallacy; acknowledge implicit assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of taking "some professedly-simple datum" and assuming nothing beyond it: such restriction indirectly smuggles in many tacit assumptions (existence other than alleged, quantity, number, limit, difference, likeness, class, attribute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting out philosophical arguments, do not pretend to assume only a single simple datum without recognizing complementary and correlative thoughts implicitly present. Explicitly examine and state tacit assumptions; otherwise reasoning will be circular. The correct procedure is to provisionally accept the fundamental intuitions essential to thought, while leaving their ultimate justification to be determined by the results of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic nature of thought: every thought implies a system
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every thought involves a whole system of thoughts, and ceases to exist if severed from its various correlatives... we cannot cut out one, and proceed as though it had survived the separation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical analysis must respect the interdependence of concepts. Isolating a concept as if independent (like isolating an organ from a living body) is a methodological error. Analyses should account for correlatives and the network of ideas that give any concept its meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to utter highest truth as part of social agency
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whoever hesitates to utter that which he thinks the highest truth... may reassure himself by looking at his acts from an impersonal point of view... he may properly give full utterance to his innermost conviction... he is a parent of the future; his thoughts are as children born to him."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophers and thinkers are authorized and morally permitted to express their deepest convictions even when those convictions seem ahead of their time, because individual opinions contribute to social change. Express belief candidly but responsibly, leaving effects to follow; this is part of the agent's role in the evolution of ideas. This guidance is tempered by the earlier injunction to temper antagonism with sympathy and toleration.
